hero.label: Made for Postal
hero.headline: I want to be Postal's first sales hire and help build the playbook.
hero.subheadline: Postal is solving a genuinely underserved problem: businesses drowning in physical mail and compliance chaos have no good modern option. I spent over a year doing cold outreach and pipeline building at an AI startup, and I know how to find the customers who feel that pain most acutely. A four-person YC-backed team at this exact stage is where I want to be.

whyCompany.title: Compliance mail is a real, urgent pain point with no obvious incumbent winner
whyCompany.body: Most businesses handling licensing filings, insurance renewals, and regulatory mail are still doing it manually or missing deadlines entirely. Postal's AI-native approach to triaging and routing that work is a clear wedge into a market where the status quo is genuinely broken. That means the sales conversation writes itself once you reach the right buyer.

whyCompany.title: Four employees, one open sales role, and a YC pedigree behind it
whyCompany.body: Postal is at the exact moment where the first dedicated sales motion gets built from scratch, and whoever holds that role shapes how the company grows. Being the founding SDR at a W22 YC company with a small, focused team means real ownership over process, messaging, and early customer relationships. That is not a support role; it is a builder role.

whyCompany.title: My BDR experience at an AI startup maps directly onto what Postal needs right now
whyCompany.body: At Copygen.ai I ran cold outreach end to end using HubSpot and LinkedIn sequences and helped bring in 15 to 20 paying clients for a product that also required explaining a new category to skeptical buyers. At NextAfter I worked inside a B2B consultancy learning how to communicate value to decision-makers who care about ROI, not features. Postal's ICP, whether that is ops leads, CFOs, or compliance managers, is exactly the kind of buyer I have been trained to reach.

quote: I have already built pipeline for an AI product from zero, and I want to do it again at a company where the problem is this obvious and the team is this small. This is the role where I can actually matter on day one.
